checks.rationale: The five local actions cover the assigned Bru-Seq route and retain its genuine interfaces: cellular pulse, extracted total RNA, antibody-bead-bound RNA, released RNA and physical cDNA library. The two extra material inputs are a labeling reagent and capture support, not extra workflows. The two multi-input operations denote genuine joint labeling/capture, each with one resulting preparation; neither collapses independent branches. Unlabeled strands in the isolation cartoon are constituents of one preparation, not separately collected fractions. The neighboring poster rows and isolated chemical drawings create no in-scope branch. The primary-supported relocation of fragmentation is implemented inside the existing broad library block, without inventing an intervening isolated fraction or a sequencing/data operation.

checks.rationale: The image caption Single strand library prep is preserved as a source observation. It does not establish final library strandedness. The registered protocol explicitly includes first-strand synthesis for strand specificity, dU-containing second-strand synthesis, ds cDNA recovery, adaptor ligation and uridine digestion/enrichment. Calling the output a strand-specific cDNA sequencing library is supported; the graph and properties make no claim that the final product is single-stranded DNA or bromouridine-bearing RNA. Keeping these actions within the broad depicted library block is appropriate.

source_sections.text:
Bru-Seq maps nascent RNA transcripts using bromouridine tagging. Active RNAPII synthesizes RNA in the presence of Br-UTP. Tagged RNA transcripts are immunoseparated from total RNA using magnetic beads coated with anti-BrdU antibodies. The captured RNA transcripts are eluted and fragmented before synthesis of cDNA strands via RT and PCR amplification. The resultant cDNA strands are prepared for sequencing using an Illumina TruSeq RNA Library Prep Kit.
Pros:
Maps sequences of nascent RNA transcripts and determines relative transcription rate
Detects lncRNAs1
Detects transcription anywhere on the genome
Cons:
Limited to cell cultures and other artificial systems, due to the requirement for incubation in the presence of labeled nucleotides
